Clique expansion of a hypergraph

Source: R/clique_expansion.R
clique_expansion.Rd

clique_expansion() projects a hypergraph onto an ordinary pairwise network, its clique expansion (also called the "downgrade" of a hypergraph to a dyadic graph): each hyperedge links every pair of its members, and the weight between two nodes sums these links over the hyperedges. It takes a net_hypergraph from build_hypergraph() or bipartite_groups() and returns an undirected netobject. With binary incidence, the weight W[i, j] is the number of hyperedges containing both i and j; with weighted incidence, it is the sum over hyperedges of the product of the two members' incidence values.

The projection keeps which pairs co-occur and how often, and drops the groups themselves: three hyperedges {A, B}, {B, C} and {A, C} give the same network as one hyperedge {A, B, C}. Read its edges as pairwise co-occurrence; hypergraph_measures() and hypergraph_centrality() work on the groups.

Usage

clique_expansion(hg, weighted = TRUE)

Arguments

hg

The hypergraph: a net_hypergraph from build_hypergraph() or bipartite_groups().

weighted

Whether to use the hypergraph's incidence values. With TRUE (default), a weighted hypergraph (from bipartite_groups() with weight) gives a weighted projection; with FALSE, the incidence is binarised first, so each weight counts the hyperedges the pair shares. For an unweighted hypergraph the two agree.

Value

A netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network")) with method "clique_expansion", undirected. print(), summary(), extract_edges(), net_centrality() and cograph::splot() read it as any network from build_network(). It carries no data, so the resampling verbs, such as bootstrap_network(), and sequence clustering refuse it. Its weight matrix is W = incidence %*% t(incidence) with a zero diagonal, and it holds the standard netobject fields (weights, nodes, edges, n_nodes, n_edges, meta). edges has one row per non-zero upper-triangle cell, with integer from/to node indices and weight. params records source, weighted, n_hyperedges and hypergraph_size_distribution.

Details

The weight matrix is computed in one BLAS call, tcrossprod(incidence), in O(n_nodes^2 * n_hyperedges) time. With binary incidence (an unweighted hypergraph, or weighted = FALSE), its off-diagonal counts are those of cooccurrence() on the same groups, which also keeps the diagonal.

Note

Experimental. Validated against tcrossprod(incidence) with a zero diagonal. No external R package exposes clique expansion as a primitive; the implementation restates the definition in one line.

References

Tian, H., & Zafarani, R. (2024). Higher-order networks representation and learning: A survey. ACM SIGKDD Explorations Newsletter 26(1), 1-18.

See also

build_hypergraph(), bipartite_groups(), build_network().

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hg  <- bipartite_groups(df, player = "player", group = "session")
net <- clique_expansion(hg)
extract_edges(net, threshold = 1)
#>   from to weight
#> 1    A  B      2
